events.type: industry / macro: AI-spending doubt hits chip stocks (no company news)
events.summary: AXT fell 10.19% to $71.66 on Thursday on 10.13 million shares (about 1.24 times its 20-day average). It opened 3.41% lower at $77.07 and slid another 7.02% from the open to the close. That day a Financial Times report said OpenAI's annualized revenue was about $20 billion less than the company had previously signaled; chipmakers fell 3.4% and the S&P 500 fell 0.47% and the Nasdaq 1.25% (Reuters). Oil also jumped (WTI +3.6%, Brent +4.1%) on Middle East tensions and hurricane-related US output cuts, which stoked inflation and rate-hike fears (Reuters). Optical suppliers fell hardest: AAOI -13.58%, Lumentum -5.62%, VIAVI -4.71% (data/prices); 24/7 Wall St. called it profit-taking after big yearly runs (AAOI +221% and Lumentum +190% year to date). Move attribution: market -0.70 points, chip industry -4.67, AXT's own -4.82 (z-score -0.57, inside its normal day-to-day noise). No AXT filing, press release, analyst downgrade or China news was found for the day.
events.why_it_matters: It shows how AXT trades: as the most leveraged bet on AI optical spending. When news casts doubt on whether AI buyers can keep paying (OpenAI's revenue), AXT falls about twice as much as the chip index. Nothing in the business changed.

events.type: price move with no published cause (company-specific fade)
events.summary: AXT fell another 4.47% to $68.46 on Friday while optical peers rose (Lumentum +5.2%, AAOI +3.5%, VIAVI +3.1%). Tech rebounded after Bloomberg reported OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70 billion of annualized revenue (Yahoo Finance live blog). AXT opened 2.87% higher at $73.71, reached $75.49, then sank to close at $68.46, near the day's low of $68.20: -7.13% from open to close and -9.31% from the high (data/prices). Chip stocks also gave back their early gains (SMH opened about +1.3% and closed -0.65%; open-to-close -1.92%), but AXT's fade was far bigger than its optical peers' (open-to-close: AAOI -2.66%, Lumentum -1.09%, VIAVI -0.08%; data/prices). Volume 8.70 million (1.05 times the 20-day average). Attribution: market +0.98, industry -2.44, AXT's own -3.01 (z -0.35, normal). It was AXT's fourth straight daily fall, and the first close below its 50-day average ($71.61) since 2026-09-15. No filing, press release, analyst action or China/export news was found for the day.
events.why_it_matters: The part that is AXT's own has no published explanation. Over five days AXT is down 20.27%, of which -11.46 points are company-specific (z -0.6). That is large in dollars but still within AXT's normal noise, because its typical company-specific day is about 8.5%.

events.summary: GuruFocus (07:58 on 10-08) reported that Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson said China's push for better optical components and faster networks could favor suppliers like AXT, because China wants optical solutions that Western competitors cannot fully meet. No rating or price-target change was reported. Only one tier-3 source; the Wedbush note itself was not found.
events.why_it_matters: A mildly positive opinion, not a fact. Chinese optical makers buying more InP wafers would not need US-bound export permits, but this is not confirmed. AXT already has one Chinese prepaid customer: Nanjing Casela, about $25.4m committed for 2027 (8-K of 2026-06-17).

why_chain.text: Thursday: AXT fell 10.19%. Market -0.70 points, chip industry -4.67, AXT's own -4.82 (z -0.57). About half the fall is explained by the market and chip stocks; the other half is AXT's own but inside its normal range.

Chip stocks fell on Thursday (chipmakers -3.4%; SMH -2.84%) after a Financial Times report said OpenAI's annualized revenue was about $20bn less than it had signaled. That revived worries that the AI spending spree is getting harder to justify. Rising oil (Brent +4.1%) added inflation and rate-hike fears.
Optical suppliers, AXT's customers and peers, fell more than chips (AAOI -13.58%, Lumentum -5.62%). Coverage called it profit-taking after very large yearly gains.

AXT amplifies these moves. The attribution model gives it a market beta of 1.64 and a chip-industry beta of 1.95, its one-year beta to the market is 4.29, and it is valued at a high multiple of its sales (Zacks put it at 42.5 times trailing sales on 2026-10-07). Stocks priced on years of future growth fall most when doubts arise about who will pay for that growth.

Basic driver: AXT's share price is a bet that AI data centers will keep buying ever more laser-based optical links, built on InP wafers. OpenAI is one of the biggest buyers of AI computing, and its revenue is what ultimately pays for the data centers. A report that it earns less than thought lowers the expected size of that future, and the most leveraged bets reprice first.

Friday: the OpenAI worry eased (Bloomberg reported OpenAI expects at least $70bn annualized revenue) and optical peers rebounded. AXT opened +2.87% but closed -4.47%, near the day's low. Chip stocks also faded intraday (SMH open-to-close -1.92%), which explains part of it; no published reason was found for the chip fade.

Why AXT faded much more than optical peers on Friday is not explained by any source: no filing, press release, analyst action or China/export news was found. Possible but unproven: continued selling of the most volatile name ahead of 10-29 results; technical selling once it broke below its 50-day average ($71.61); and AXT's China exposure (permit risk, the 2026-11-27 gallium/germanium date) making it a less natural 'buy the dip' than US-based optical makers.

products.name: Indium phosphide (InP) wafer substrates
products.what_it_is: Thin, polished discs of indium phosphide crystal on which laser and photodetector chips for optical data links are built.
products.analogy: The blank canvas a painter must buy before painting: Lumentum or Coherent 'paint' the lasers onto AXT's canvas.
products.buyers: Laser and optical-chip makers. Disclosed prepaid customers: Lumentum (six-year deal, two $43.5m deposits), Coherent (about $22.3m prepayment) and China's Nanjing Casela (RMB 173m, about $25.4m, committed for 2027 with 50% prepaid).
products.how_it_works: AXT grows InP crystals in its Chinese factories (subsidiary Tongmei), slices them into wafers and polishes them. Customers grow thin layers on the wafers and pattern them into lasers that turn electrical signals into light for AI data-center links. Exports from China need a Ministry of Commerce permit for each shipment.
products.sales: InP revenue $30.7m in Q2 2026, out of $47.6m total revenue (Q2 call, tier 3); InP backlog above $100m (Q2 call). Total Q2 revenue $47.6m (company release, tier 1). Q3 total guidance about $66m (call).
products.sales_source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1051627/000143774926025061/ex_974537.htm (total revenue, tier 1); https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/03/axt-axti-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/ (InP split, backlog and guidance, tier 3 transcript); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001051627/000143774926024883/axti20260715_8k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001051627/000143774926022557/axti20260630_8k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1051627/000143774926020978/axti20260615_8k.htm
products.stage: shipping, ramping in volume (capacity being added); shipments to US customers limited by Chinese export permits
products.size_for_company: About 64% of Q2 revenue ($30.7m of $47.6m), and the main growth driver.
products.competition: Japan's Sumitomo Electric and JX Advanced Metals, both expanding InP capacity (JX up to 10 times by FY2030; Sumitomo spending JPY 18bn); some laser makers also grow their own material. No new competitor news in the window.
products.why_investors_care: Few companies make InP wafers at scale, and AI optics demand has made them scarce. That is why customers prepay, and it is the core of both thesis statements.
products.watch_next: Q3 InP revenue and backlog on 2026-10-29; any update on export permits for US customers; new prepaid deals.
